1.why: Body text uses a clean sans-serif at a adequate size with comfortable line height and whitespace between blocks, though letter spacing appears default rather than notably generous.

2.why: All headings, labels, and instructions are short sentence-case strings with no italics, no all-caps text, and no dense paragraphs on any screen.

3.why: The single-column, mobile-width layout with full-width inputs and clear vertical stacking reads well, with only the smaller 'Logs' type as a minor legibility drawback.

4.why: Each screen's instruction is a single plain sentence, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code delivered to your verified mobile number.'

5.why: No field shows a placeholder or worked example of the expected input; the only format cue is the phrase 'six-digit', leaving users to infer the rest.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a single sentence, so the user never has to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The verification code must be typed by hand and no copy affordance or copyable secret is presented anywhere in the observed flow, including no recovery-code screen at all.

8.why: Manual entry is the only method offered on every screen; no QR code or equivalent alternative appears anywhere in the flow.

9.why: The email, phone, and code fields are plain text inputs with no visible autocomplete or one-time-code hints and no observed password-manager or autofill integration.

10.why: A bold heading names the current step and a single solid-blue button (with a visible focus ring after the error) marks the primary action, though no overall progress indicator is provided.

11.why: Each screen requests exactly one main action ('Continue' or 'Verify identity'), with step 1's two fields submitted together under that single action.

12.why: The log line 'Identity verification delivery was initiated' and the next-screen instruction give some feedback, but the wording is system-centric and the error state does not plainly explain what happened.

13.why: After the failed attempt the form stays active and invites retry with no visible penalty, although no reveal/hide or re-request/resend controls are offered.

14.why: The red message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blame and suggests retrying but never states the actual problem, such as an incorrect code.

15.why: No countdown, expiry notice, or session timer appears on any screen, so reading is untimed and code entry shows no visible time pressure.
